newsitem.title: PERU: Peru GDP to fall under new calculation - gov't.
newsitem.headline: Peru GDP to fall under new calculation - gov't.

text.p: Peru's new measure of gross domestic product (GDP) will reduce the current over-valued total of $60 billion to between $50 billion and $51 billion, Economy Ministry officials said Wednesday.
The current measure takes a base year of 1979 for the indices used in the GDP calculation, but analysts and government officials agree this has caused a distortion in the overall figure.
The new calculation -- which will take 1994 as the base year -- will be used from August, the ministry officials said in an interview.
Overall GDP is likely to rise in 1997 slightly more than the formal government projection of 2.5 percent, they added.

According to latest figures, GDP grew 2.2 percent in the first 11 months of 1996, and is expected to end the year at around 2.5 percent, compared to an annual total of 7.0 percent in 1995. The official 1996 figure is due to be announced next week.
